items.title: Micron Stays Flat as 68-Month Bonuses Fail to End Strike Risk
items.summary: Record memory profits produced extraordinary rewards, but approximately 10,000 Taiwanese workers remain represented by unions threatening action.

items.title: Storage Stocks Slide as Profit Taking Follows Big Run: Seagate Falls 4%, SanDisk Drops 3%, Micron Holds Flat
items.summary: Seagate just gave back a chunk of its monster year-to-date run with no news attached, and the reason Micron is doing the opposite tells you everything about where the smart money actually sits in memory right now.

items.title: Why Micron Stock Is on Pace for a Weekly Decline
items.summary: The question for investors is how Micron stock will perform in the run-up to fiscal fourth-quarter earnings on Sept. 30.

items.title: Wall Street Just Erased $57 Billion From Micron. The Shortage Behind Its Boom Is Getting Worse.
items.summary: Micron just posted the highest revenue guidance in its history while the shortage fueling its growth gets worse, yet Wall Street wiped out tens of billions in market cap anyway. The signal hiding inside that contradiction is worth understanding before the next move.

items.title: Micron’s Powerful Economics 101 Lesson Keeps Me Buying
items.summary: Three companies control the world's DRAM supply, AI is burning through memory faster than fabs can build it, and one of those three just signed contracts that could permanently rewire what a chip cycle looks like.

items.title: Micron Just Made a $32,000 Move as Taiwan Labor Pressure Builds
items.summary: Record profits are giving Micron's engineers more leverage over what they get paid.

items.title: Prediction: This AI Stock Could Be the Next One to Shock Wall Street
items.summary: Micron has already stunned Wall Street with a historic surge, but a fresh competitive threat just knocked shares down and reignited the debate over whether the AI memory trade still has legs or has finally run out of road.

items.title: How Far Could Intel Stock Fall After More Than Quadrupling In A Year?
items.summary: Intel (INTC) stock fell 5.6% on September 10 and trades near $100, about 29% below its 52-week high. Even so, it has returned 310.5% over the past year. The question is how much of that a market shock could take back, and on average Intel has fallen harder than the S&P 500 when shocks hit.
